title: Αἴξ καὶ αἰγοβοσκός
part: The Goat and the Goatherd (Chambry 15 · Perry 280)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 15 (= Perry 280). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Αἰγοβοσκὸς τὰς αἶγας ἀνεκαλεῖτο πρὸς τὴν μάνδραν.
sentences.tr: Aigoboskos tas aigas anekaleito pros tēn mandran.
sentences.l: A goatherd was calling his goats back to the pen.
sentences.n: αἰγοβοσκός is transparent — αἴξ “goat” + βόσκω “feed, pasture”, the goat-feeder. A μάνδρα is the walled fold the animals are shut into for the night.

sentences.t: Μία δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ὑπελείφθη, ἡδύ τι βοσκομένη.
sentences.tr: Mia de ex autōn hypeleiphthē, hēdy ti boskomenē.
sentences.l: But one of them was left behind, feeding on something sweet.
sentences.i: One of them stayed behind, browsing on something she liked.
sentences.n: ἡδύ τι is the object of the middle βοσκομένη — “grazing on something nice”. The active βόσκω is what the herdsman does to the flock, the middle what the animal does for itself; the same verb stands behind his name in the line above.

sentences.t: Ῥίψας δ’ ὁ ποιμὴν πέτραν τὸ κέρας αὐτῆς κατέαξεν εὐστοχήσας.
sentences.tr: Rhipsas d' ho poimēn petran to keras autēs kateaxen eustochēsas.
sentences.l: And the shepherd, having thrown a stone, shattered her horn, having aimed well.
sentences.i: The herdsman threw a stone and, aiming only too well, shattered her horn.
sentences.n: The sentence is framed by two participles, one before the verb and one after it, so the aim is reported last, as an afterthought. κατέαξεν, from κατάγνυμι, is “broke clean through”. εὐστοχέω is ordinarily a word of praise — to hit what one aims at — and is used here of damage he did not want.

sentences.t: Ἐδυσώπει δὲ τὴν αἶγα μὴ εἰπεῖν τοῦτο τῷ δεσπότῃ.
sentences.tr: Edysōpei de tēn aiga mē eipein touto tōi despotēi.
sentences.l: And he was coaxing the goat not to tell this to the master.
sentences.i: He kept pleading with the goat not to tell the master.
sentences.n: δυσωπέω is to work on someone's face — to shame or coax them into something — and the imperfect makes it repeated pleading. μή, not οὐ, is the negative used with an infinitive after a verb of asking. The δεσπότης is the owner; the goatherd only keeps the flock, which is why he is afraid.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· « Κἂν ἐγὼ σιωπήσω, πῶς κρύψω ; πρόδηλον γάρ ἐστι πᾶσι τὸ κέρας μου κεκλασμένον. »
sentences.tr: Hē de eipen: « Kan egō siōpēsō, pōs krypsō ; prodēlon gar esti pasi to keras mou keklasmenon. »
sentences.l: And she said: « Even if I keep silent, how am I to hide it? For plain to all is my horn, broken. »
sentences.i: She said, « Even if I say nothing, how am I to hide it? My broken horn is there for everyone to see. »
sentences.n: The Greek question mark is the semicolon ;, printed here with the space before it that Chambry's French typesetting gives it. κρύψω is the same in form for the future indicative and the aorist subjunctive; after πῶς the deliberative subjunctive is the likelier reading — “how am I to hide it?” κεκλασμένον is a perfect participle: the horn is not breaking, it stands broken, and that state is what everyone can see.

sentences.t: Ὅτι, τῆς αἰτίας προδήλου οὔσης, οὐ δυνατὸν ταύτην καλύψαι.
sentences.tr: Hoti, tēs aitias prodēlou ousēs, ou dynaton tautēn kalypsai.
sentences.l: That, the cause being manifest, it is not possible to hide it.
sentences.i: That when the cause is out in the open, there is no hiding it.
sentences.n: The bare-Ὅτι moral formula: the opening words (ὁ μῦθος δηλοῖ, “the fable shows”) are simply left off and the ὅτι-clause stands alone. It recurs across this collection. τῆς αἰτίας … οὔσης is a genitive absolute. αἰτία covers both the cause of a thing and the blame for it, and the fable turns on holding the two together: what caused the break is exactly what fixes the fault.
